splitProposalChirho.criteriaChirho: Concrete physical route or path for travel — Matt 2:12 'another way', Matt 4:15 'way of the sea', Matt 8:28, Matt 13:4 'along the path', Matt 20:17, 30; the journey sense Luke 11:6

splitProposalChirho.newLabelChirho: way of life, course of conduct
splitProposalChirho.criteriaChirho: Figurative moral or spiritual way — Matt 3:3 'prepare the way of the Lord', Matt 7:13-14 'narrow/broad way', Matt 22:16 'way of God', Matt 21:32 'way of righteousness', John 14:6 'I am the way'

reasoningChirho: The description explicitly combines 'the literal meaning of a physical road, way, or path and the figurative meaning of a way of life or course of conduct.' This is a classic case of concrete vs. abstract meanings that should be distinguished. The literal uses refer to actual physical routes (road to Egypt, path along which seed falls), while figurative uses refer to moral/spiritual direction (way of righteousness, way of the Lord). Cross-linguistic evidence supports the distinction: the same surface form spans two conceptually distinct semantic domains — physical space vs. moral conduct. The LIFE IS A JOURNEY metaphor has been fully lexicalized here but still represents two distinct senses.
